title: Open-loop cost control and eval runbook for low-cost inference variants
content:
Purpose
This is a working runbook for how we instrument, evaluate, and gate low-cost inference variants (i.e., model quantization + lighter decoders + smaller context routing) before and during traffic ramp. The goal is to provide an operationally simple, repeatable process that balances unit-cost savings with an explicit, measurable quality-of-service (QoS) budget.

Background / motivation
- Product and infra want options to push lower-cost execution variants into production to save per-token spend.
- Historically we detect quality regressions too late (after customer complaints or metric drift), which makes rollbacks blunt and costly.
- We need a systematic eval + gate framework that: 1) quantifies cost-of-quality tradeoffs up front, 2) allocates an evaluation budget and sampling plan, and 3) enforces automated gates tied to observable metrics.

High-level requirements
- Make the gating logic data-driven and auditable (easy to backfill what triggered fallback).
- Keep human-in-the-loop for early-stage experiments; automated enforcement for scaled rollouts.
- Support multiple failure modes: semantic regressions, hallucination spike, short-form fluency loss, severe latency tail regressions.
- Integrate with existing rollout primitives (canary routing, A/B, auto-fallback to baseline variant).

Definitions (quick)
- Baseline: the current production model/runner we treat as the quality reference.
- Low-cost variant: any configuration expected to reduce unit cost (different weights, quantization, smaller context window, alternative kernel).
- Eval budget: number of samples (requests) and human-labeling allowance reserved for a trial.
- Gate: a rule (statistical threshold + action) that blocks further ramp or triggers fallback.

Suggested evaluation process
1) Offline profiling (day -7 to -2)
   - Run the variant over a representative historical sample (1–5M tokens depending on workload) to compute per-token cost delta, latency distribution differences, and automatic proxies (perplexity, length-normalized log-prob).
   - Produce a small candidate set of guardrail metrics (see spreadsheet columns below).
   - If offline proxies show >5% degradation on primary proxy, mark as high-risk and require extra human review.

2) Small closed beta (day -2 to day 0)
   - Route 0.1%–0.5% of live traffic to variant for a short warm-up (24–72h).
   - Sample requests across user cohorts proportional to traffic; ensure heavy-tailed and long-context signals are included.
   - Automatic instrumentation: token-level cost, top-k logit drift, response length, latency p50/p95/p99, safety classifier hits, hallucination proxy score.
   - Human-in-the-loop: sample N requests per day to label for semantic correctness and safety (N depends on eval budget; default 200/day).

3) Controlled ramp (day 1–7)
   - If closed beta passes gates, ramp to 1% → 5% → 20% with hold windows at each step. Each hold must pass automated gates for a minimum observation window (e.g., 24h with at least M labeled samples).
   - If any gate trips, automatic fallback to baseline and current rollout is aborted; document incident and run deeper diffs.

Spreadsheet design (columns to include in the cost model sheet)
- variant_id (string)
- baseline_id (string)
- expected_unit_cost_delta_pct (numeric-string e.g., "-12.5%")
- measured_unit_cost_delta_pct_live (string)
- offline_proxy_delta_pct (string)
- p50_latency_delta_ms, p95_delta_ms, p99_delta_ms (strings)
- auto-safety-hits_delta_pct (string)
- hallucination_proxy_delta (string)
- semantic-f1_delta_pct (string) -- when labeled test exists
- sample_count_live (string)
- labeled_samples_count (string)
- eval_budget_used (string, e.g. "230/1000 human labels")
- gating_status (string: "pass" | "warn" | "fail")
- gate_trigger_reason (string)
- next_action (string: "ramp" | "hold" | "rollback" | "investigate")
- notes (string)

Notes on proxies and labels
- We expect proxies (perplexity, log-prob deltas, classifier scores) to have imperfect correlation with human labels. Calibration is required per workload. Keep calibration metadata in a separate sheet (mapping proxy thresholds to expected human-F1).
- Human labeling strategy: prioritize examples where proxies disagree strongly with baseline (high delta), and examples from high-value customers or churn-sensitive routes.

Gate proposals (conservative default)
- Safety gate: if safety classifier hits increase by >10% relative or absolute rate crosses a critical threshold, immediate rollback.
- Semantic gate: if human-labeled semantic F1 drops >3 points or relative drop >5% (whichever smaller), fail.
- Latency gate: if p99 increases by >200ms and p95 by >100ms, fail.
- Economic gate: if unit cost reduction is <1% net after considering extra human evaluation cost, mark as "economically weak" (warn) and require product sign-off.
- Accumulated small regressions gate: if three different proxies each cross a lower threshold (e.g., 1–2% degradation), escalate to human review.

Statistical considerations and sampling rules
- Use weighted sampling to ensure tail behaviors are captured: sample more heavily from long-context (>2k token) requests and from routes flagged by product as high-sensitivity.
- For semantic labels, maintain cohort-level confidence intervals; require minimum labeled sample count (default 200) per hold window to consider semantic gate as evaluated.
- Apply sequential testing corrections for multiple intermediate checks (alpha-spending). We recommend using a conservative sequential test (e.g., Pocock boundary) for automated gating decisions during ramp.

Ops playbook for a gate trip (quick runbook)
1) Automatic action triggers fallback and opens incident in PagerDuty + auto-notify product/eng-optimize channel.
2) Triage owner (on-call product-ops or experiment owner) evaluates: examine top failing examples, run differential prompts against baseline, check hardware/network anomalies.
3) If issue is model-derived (quality), pause all ramps and schedule deep-labeling batch (1k prioritized samples).
4) If transient infra noise (latency spike from node), allow infra rollback and resume variant after confirmation.
5) Post-mortem: update spreadsheet with root cause, corrective action, and decide whether threshold tuning is needed.

Cost accounting and break-even calculus (simple)
- For each variant compute: net_savings = baseline_cost_per_request * traffic_fraction * 30d * savings_pct - labeling_cost - operational_incident_cost_estimate.
- Labeling_cost = human_label_cost_per_sample * labeled_samples_count in the test horizon. Use conservative human_label_cost_per_sample = $8 for semantic labeling for now.
- Incident_cost_estimate: we maintain a rolling estimate from past incidents (default $3k for small rollouts, escalate with enterprise routes).

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide
- How aggressive should the economic gate be for enterprise routes with SLA credits? (suggest higher bar: require >3% unit savings).
- Where to store and version calibration data for proxies? (confluence vs. small DB)
- Who signs off on "warn" items to proceed—product manager or on-call SRE?
- Should we invest in a small active-learning loop to reduce human labeling costs for future variants?

Next immediate actions (owner: Asha)
- Build the suggested spreadsheet skeleton under product optimize drive and populate with data from the last 3 variant experiments (ENG-1297, ENG-1384) — target 2026-03-12.
- Wire the gating_status field into rollout telemetry so canary UI shows pass/warn/fail (engineering ticket: ENG-1452).
- Schedule a 60-min sync with SRE and solutions-eng to align sampling rules (week of 2026-03-15).

TODOs (short)
- [ ] Finalize default thresholds for proxies per workload class (chat vs embedding vs rerank).
- [ ] Add mapping of proxy->expected-label-F1 to the spreadsheet.
- [ ] Add costs from labeling vendor and update economic gate formula.
- [ ] Draft an internal one-pager for sales/CS explaining what "low-cost variants" mean for enterprise SLAs.

Notes to self:
- Keep the runbook light: we want to enable many small experiments without CTO-level signoff, but enforce clear automated stop conditions.
- Where possible, surface the exact failing examples in the rollout UI so PMs can triage quickly.
